sites.name: Mogao Caves, Dunhuang: 2026 visiting rules
sites.what: Regional access rules from the Dunhuang Academy's 2026 opening notice; the site itself is held on China's record.

access.opening: 1 April to 30 November 8 am to 6 pm (last entry 4.10 pm); 1 December to 31 March 9 am to 5 pm (last entry 3.10 pm)
access.tickets: Real-name timed booking; standard visit capped at 6,000 a day (digital films plus 8 caves). Foreign passport holders book on the 莫高窟参观预约网 WeChat account, 'Ticket Booking' menu; the Academy authorises no third-party sellers. Arrive at the Mogao Digital Exhibition Center 30 minutes before your slot with the same passport.
access.photography: Photography and filming inside the caves is banned; suitcases and bags 20 inches or larger may not be taken into the cave area.
access.closures: Caves close in heavy rain or sandstorms, with full refunds for unused tickets.

lore.text: Local legend says the monk Le Zun began the caves in 366 after seeing a vision of a thousand Buddhas in golden light on the cliff.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source

ancient-sites-and-mysteries.evidence: Official pages; read directly unless marked search snapshot.

laws.rule: At the Mogao Caves, taking photos inside the caves, and scratching, writing on or touching murals and painted sculptures, is forbidden. Unapproved live streaming or recording in the caves, cinema, exhibition halls and visitor routes is also not allowed.
At the Mogao Caves, large luggage, pets and drones may not be taken into the cave area.

layers.process: Mogao Caves tickets are booked online through the Dunhuang Academy's ticketing service; online booking hours are 07:00 to 22:00. Entry starts at the Digital Exhibition Centre, where the ticket sheet is checked, and again at the cave area. Peak season (1 April to 30 November): standard visit of a digital film plus 8 caves, CNY 238 (about A$51). Off-season (1 December to 31 March): CNY 140 (about A$30) for the film plus 10 caves. An emergency visit of 4 caves is CNY 100 (about A$21). Rate: A$1 = CNY 4.6877, RBA 30 Oct 2026. The page publishes no daily cap figure.
